section: Red flags: 2023 decision not to show Erwin Wurm's Fat Car works
problems: changed detail: 'in the title' is not on the page; Wurm's reason is given as 'the word fat'
before:
Red flags: 2023 decision not to show Erwin Wurm's Fat Car works
- Erwin Wurm's exhibition at Yorkshire Sculpture Park, running until 28 April 2024, left out his Fat Car series, real cars coated in plastic with a layer of polyester (The Art Newspaper, 3 July 2023).
- Wurm said of the park, "They do not want to show them", and said he believed the reason was the word "fat" in the title (The Art Newspaper, relaying his remarks to the Telegraph).
- The director, Clare Lilley, said "there was real disquiet from members of staff about how they could interpret those works in a positive way to our audience" and "I think that it is right that we're sensitive to the hurt that people would inevitably feel" (The Art Newspaper).
after:
Red flags: 2023 decision not to show Erwin Wurm's Fat Car works
- Erwin Wurm's exhibition at Yorkshire Sculpture Park, running until 28 April 2024, left out his Fat Car series, real cars coated in plastic with a layer of polyester (The Art Newspaper, 3 July 2023).
- Wurm said of the park, "They do not want to show them", and said he believed the word "fat" was the reason (The Art Newspaper, relaying his remarks to the Telegraph).
- The director, Clare Lilley, said "there was real disquiet from members of staff about how they could interpret those works in a positive way to our audience" and "I think that it is right that we're sensitive to the hurt that people would inevitably feel" (The Art Newspaper).
reason: The Art Newspaper diary item (3 July 2023) opened; it carries Wurm's objection ('They do not want to show them') and Lilley's reply word for word. A work left out by the space over staff disquiet, with the artist objecting, dated after November 2021, stays under Red flags.

problems: missing year: the page dates the Avery Road plan and hearing to 2012
changed detail: 'feeling it clashed' is not the page's wording; the page says neighbours argued it did not fit the road's character
order: Olnick's quote was said at the hearing, before the move
Calabrese named without his role; the page calls him Magazzino's director
before:
WIDER CONTEXT
- Nancy Olnick and Giorgio Spanu first planned to build the museum on their estate on Avery Road. "Neighbors filled a public hearing to protest the scale of the project", feeling it clashed with the road's residential and rustic character (The Highlands Current, Alison Rooney, 23 September 2016).
- The founders put the project on hold and moved it to a site on Route 9. Olnick said "We feel the same way as the rest of the neighbors"; Calabrese said "The decision, after the 2012 situation, was to listen to the community, to relocate and not create any tensions" (The Highlands Current).
after:
WIDER CONTEXT
- In 2012 Nancy Olnick and Giorgio Spanu planned to build the museum on their estate on Avery Road. "Neighbors filled a public hearing to protest the scale of the project", which they argued did not fit the residential and rustic character of the road. At the hearing Olnick said, "We feel the same way as the rest of the neighbors" (The Highlands Current, Alison Rooney, 23 September 2016).
- After the hearing the founders put the project on hold and later built it on Route 9. Magazzino's director, Vittorio Calabrese, said: "The decision, after the 2012 situation, was to listen to the community, to relocate and not create any tensions" (The Highlands Current).
reason: Highlands Current page opened; every point is on it. 2012 neighbourhood opposition to the museum's first site, so WIDER CONTEXT.

problems: repeats record: the reflected light's effect on gallery conditions is already in the record's Hyperallergic point; first point cut back to the dispute
'about 18 months' is '18 months' on the page
unsupported: 'did not fully solve the problem' replaced with the spokesperson's words from the page
AAMD quotation trimmed to the parts that concern the Nasher
before:
WIDER CONTEXT
- The Nasher Sculpture Center said sunlight reflected from Museum Tower disrupted the controlled environment of its galleries and garden and endangered its collection; by February 2013 the two sides had failed to agree for about 18 months (CultureMap Dallas, Jennifer Chininis, 13 February 2013).
- In November 2012 Museum Tower's owners rejected the Nasher's proposed louver solution as unattractive and unacceptable to homebuyers. The Nasher put up temporary mesh panels for an exhibition, which it said did not fully solve the problem (CultureMap Dallas).
- The Association of Art Museum Directors issued a statement on the deadlock, saying "[t]he Association of Art Museum Directors considers the preservation and care of collections to be a paramount responsibility" and that it hoped "all parties will work together for an acceptable solution"; it said the Nasher had negotiated in good faith (CultureMap Dallas).
after:
WIDER CONTEXT
- By February 2013 the Nasher Sculpture Center and Museum Tower had been unable to agree in 18 months on a solution to the sunlight from the tower, which the Nasher contends disrupts its controlled environment and threatens works in the garden and galleries (CultureMap Dallas, Jennifer Chininis, 13 February 2013).
- In November 2012 Museum Tower rejected the Nasher's proposed louver solution as unattractive, unpleasant and unacceptable to homebuyers. The Nasher installed mesh panels on its windows and glass roof for exhibitions in 2012 and 2013; its spokesperson Jill Magnuson said they "come nowhere close to eliminating the blinding light effects in our galleries" (CultureMap Dallas).
- The Association of Art Museum Directors issued a statement "expressing concern" over the "impasse", saying the Nasher "has negotiated in good faith with the developers of Museum Tower" and that it hoped "all parties will work together for an acceptable solution" (CultureMap Dallas).
reason: CultureMap (13 February 2013, Jennifer Chininis) opened; all kept points are on it. The record holds only Hyperallergic's piece on the tower's effects; this adds the dispute itself and the AAMD statement. Before November 2021, so WIDER CONTEXT.

problems: changed detail: 'nearly no-cost rent' is 'essentially free rent' on the page
the statement says the board decided; added
before:
WIDER CONTEXT
- In June 2014 Presidio County commissioners agreed to send Ballroom Marfa a "notice of non-compliance" over its lease at Vizcaino Park for the planned Drive-In, saying the lease could be terminated unless the gallery set out its plans for community groups' use of the site, which the lease required in exchange for nearly no-cost rent (Marfa Public Radio, Travis Bubenik, 11 June 2014).
- The same day Ballroom said in a statement signed by Virginia Lebermann and Fairfax Dorn that "the project has outgrown the original vision" and "As of now further development of the Drive-In is indefinitely deferred" (Marfa Public Radio).
after:
WIDER CONTEXT
- In June 2014 Presidio County commissioners agreed to send Ballroom Marfa a "notice of non-compliance" over its land lease at Vizcaino Park for the planned Drive-In. The letter would advise that the lease could be terminated unless commissioners heard more of the gallery's plans for working with community groups; in exchange for essentially free rent, the gallery had agreed to let local community groups use the space (Marfa Public Radio, Travis Bubenik, 11 June 2014).
- Later that day Ballroom issued a statement signed by Virginia Lebermann and Fairfax Dorn saying the board had decided that "the project has outgrown the original vision" and "As of now further development of the Drive-In is indefinitely deferred" (Marfa Public Radio).
reason: Marfa Public Radio (11 June 2014) opened; the county's notice and Ballroom's statement are on it. Not in the record. Before November 2021, so WIDER CONTEXT.
